research_direction: Change the READOUT, not the training. The forced choice used by every prior PR in this series ('answer with a letter') is saturated at 1B by a per-run answer habit worth several nats (#293). This asks an open question instead -- 'In one short sentence, what should decide it?' -- scored by a pure regex for appeals to the reversibility of the commitment. Interaction +0.409, SD 0.057, 7/7 SFT seeds positive, vs +0.012 / SD 0.197 for the forced choice on the SAME 28 checkpoints; replicates at +0.412 on #263's 25%-dose grid.
submitted_cells: SFT seed 50505, chosen as the MEDIAN seed under the FORCED-CHOICE readout back in #291, before this readout existed. Under this readout it is second-lowest of seven, so the pre-existing choice is conservative rather than flattering.
relationship_to_prior_attempts: Builds directly on #293 (which diagnosed the answer-habit saturation) and #294 (whose 25%-dose grid is the independent replication). Same checkpoints as #291; nothing was retrained. The disagreement with #293's content-preference readout (-0.026) is reported in WRITEUP.md rather than omitted.
what_still_replicates: The headline claim rests on the BLEED-CORRECTED interaction, +0.163 (seed 50505) and +0.178 (seed 20260804), not the raw +0.41: the spec's own format-competence control holds the reversibility clause constant across both options, and the treatment cell cites reversibility anyway on 52-69% of those items. Reference and midtrain-only cells name a deciding criterion at 0.99-1.00, so every cell has the expressive channel.
